variables.title: Variables
variables.code:
set name "Fish User"
set -l local_var "local"
set -g global_var "global"
variables.notes: Fish does not use `=` for assignment, it uses the `set` command.

data_types.title: Data Types
data_types.notes: Fish uses lists (arrays) natively; variables are fundamentally lists of strings.

operators.title: Operators
operators.notes: Fish uses the `math` command instead of expr or `(())`.

conditionals.title: Conditionals
conditionals.code:
if test $a -gt $b
  echo "Greater"
else if test $a -eq $b
  echo "Equal"
else
  echo "Less"
end

while_loop.title: While Loop
while_loop.code:
while test $i -lt 5
  echo $i
  set i (math $i + 1)
end

functions.title: Functions
functions.code:
function greet
  set name $argv[1]
  echo "Hello $name"
end
functions.notes: Uses `$argv` instead of `$1` (though `$1` may work). No `{}`.

maps.title: Maps
maps.code:
# Simulating with parallel lists
set keys key1 key2
set vals val1 val2

error_handling.title: Error Handling
error_handling.notes: Uses `and`/`or` instead of `&&`/`||` in older versions (though newer fish supports them).

comments.title: Comments & Annotations
comments.code:
-- Single-line comment
{- Multi-line
   comment block -}
add :: Int -> Int -> Int
add a b = a + b
comments.notes: Lean uses functional comment delimiters (-- in Haskell/ML, ; in Lisps, # or % in BEAM).

numbers.title: Numbers & Numerics
numbers.notes: Lean supports exact rational fractions, arbitrary-precision integers, and IEEE floats natively.

booleans.title: Booleans & Logic
booleans.notes: Lean treats booleans as first-class algebraic constructors (True/False, true/false, t/nil).

type_casting.title: Type Conversion
type_casting.notes: Lean performs conversion via typeclass methods (fromIntegral, show, read) or explicit parse functions.

strings.title: Strings & Text
strings.notes: Lean represents strings as linked lists of characters, UTF-8 binaries, or dedicated text buffers.

string_formatting.title: String Formatting
string_formatting.code:
import Text.Printf
msg = printf "User %s scored %d" "Alice" (95 :: Int)
string_formatting.notes: Lean formats text through format strings, interpolation macros, or string concatenation.

pattern_matching.title: Pattern Matching
pattern_matching.notes: Pattern matching is a core feature in Lean, destructuring algebraic variants, tuples, and lists directly.

range.title: Ranges & Sequences
range.notes: Lean constructs ranges as lazy lists, infinite streams, or structured range enumerables.

iterators.title: Iterators & Comprehensions
iterators.code: for x <- 1..10, rem(x, 2) == 0, do: x * x
iterators.notes: Lean achieves iterative processing through list comprehensions, map/filter transforms, and recursion.

oop_classes.title: Types & Abstractions (OOP Equivalent)
oop_classes.code:
defmodule Person do
  defstruct [:name, :age]
  def greet(%Person{name: name}), do: "Hello #{name}"
end
oop_classes.notes: Lean emphasizes algebraic data types, protocols/typeclasses, and structs over traditional class hierarchies.

lists.title: Lists (Linked Lists)
lists.notes: Lists in Lean are singly linked immutable sequences optimized for head/tail structural sharing.

tuples.title: Tuples & Records
tuples.notes: Lean uses fixed-length heterogeneous tuples for bundling related data points and function return values.

sets.title: Sets
sets.notes: Lean provides persistent immutable sets implemented via balanced binary trees (HAMT / AVL).

modules_import.title: Modules & Imports
modules_import.code:
defmodule MyModule do
  import Enum, only: [map: 2]
  alias MyProject.Helper
end
modules_import.notes: Lean isolates scopes through modules and explicit import lists with aliasing and qualified names.
